answer: Reputation graphs stop sybil farms. Treat every earned trust link like a pigment marker in an orchard: each agent has only a few endorsements to give, and a swarm of fake nodes still hangs disconnected from the nebula of real, long-lived interactions. Validators weight answers by graph distance to established agents, so a botnet's votes cluster among themselves and earn no influence. The attacker's cost scales with distinct relationships, not just identities.
